content: In #43538, similarly as in #43224, I intend to prove compatibilities between the connecting homomorphism Ext X S.X₃ n → Ext X S.X₁ (n + 1) for Ext-groups (where S is a short exact sequence in an abelian category C) and a snake lemma type computation involving "compatible" injective resolutions of S.X₁, S.X₂ andS.X₃ which form a "horseshoe" diagram: the underlying cochain complexes of these resolutions form a degreewise split short exact sequence, etc.

In order to state this, I do not need the existence of such horseshoe diagrams, but if someone is interested in formalising something in homological algebra, they may formalize the following statement (which depends on the structure InjectiveResolution.Horseshoe defined in https://github.com/joelriou/mathlib4/blob/horseshoe-inj-extmk/Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Abelian/Injective/Horseshoe.lean):

lemma horseshoe
    {S : ShortComplex C} (hS : S.ShortExact)
    (R₁ : InjectiveResolution S.X₁) (R₃ : InjectiveResolution S.X₃) :
    ∃ (R₂ : InjectiveResolution S.X₂),
      Nonempty (Horseshoe hS R₁ R₂ R₃) := sorry

This is https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horseshoe_lemma (for injective resolutions). There were some discussion about this and an outline of the dual statement at https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/pull/12438#discussion_r1589838829

(This was also formalized in some form by @Johan Commelin and @Riccardo Brasca during the Liquid Tensor Experiment https://github.com/leanprover-community/lean-liquid/blob/master/src/for_mathlib/horseshoe.lean)

The PR #43538 is now sorry-free. The compatibility of the connecting homomorphism for Ext-groups and horseshoe diagrams of injective resolutions is https://github.com/joelriou/mathlib4/blob/679fa0e84f70572bda647d834ff73d7be588c3c3/Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Abelian/Injective/Horseshoe.lean#L203-L212
Then, the InjectiveResolution.Horseshoe API should be relatively stable, so do not hesitate "claiming" the horseshoe lemma stated above about the existence of these horseshoe diagrams.
